scientific_question: Is the task-macro endpoint contrast distributed across tasks or sensitive to removing one task?

units.primary: task mean of ten paired demos;40tasks per seed/condition
units.secondary: 400paired demos, grouped by40task; descriptive, not independent inferential replicates
units.anchors: two anchors averaged within eachdemo;800anchors are not independent repetitions

effect_definitions.T20_minus_C20: T20−C20; negative means lower T endpoint loss
effect_definitions.deltaC10to20: C20−C10; positive means C loss increased
effect_definitions.deltaT10to20: T20−T10; positive means T loss increased
effect_definitions.T0_minus_C0: unadjusted start difference; neither removed nor explained

compact_complete_task_table.meaning: 40tasks x4conditions x2seeds; all raw endpoints and effects retained

inference_limits: Raw endpoint losses remain the main comparison; baseline adjustment is reported separately.
Leave-one-task-out ranges are descriptive influence analyses, not confidence intervals or hypothesis tests.
Each leave-one-out calculation removes one task; it does not establish robustness to removing two or more tasks.
Both seeds are shown separately; seed agreement is a count, not an independence-based significance test.
No bootstrap, p-value, selected best checkpoint or selected subset is used.
C/T histories differ in temporal training support within the same demos; neither curve alone proves a causal mechanism.
Internal demo-heldout loss shares tasks and does not establish unseen-task, pretraining-independent or closed-loop behavior gains.
Loss includes25padding dimensions in H10xD32; no executed7D/translation/rotation/gripper loss is inferred.
result_claims: Numerical groups and full paired table above are computed only from the twelve verified input monitors; no result was preset.
